name: merge-spmv (merge-based CsrMV)
baseline: Intel MKL CSR SpMV; NVIDIA cuSPARSE csrmv
workload: CSR SpMV on circuit5M.mtx (5.5M rows, 59.5M nnz) on CPU and GPU
claimed_speedup: GPU 17.19 gflops vs cuSPARSE 0.38 gflops; CPU 9.42 gflops vs MKL 2.22 gflops (circuit5M)
compiler_and_flags: Intel C++ compiler with MKL (CPU); nvcc + GCC (GPU); flags not stated
tradeoffs: No preprocessing; requires Intel compiler/MKL for CPU path, CUDA cc3.5+ for GPU
caveats: Headline numbers from one pathological matrix; old library versions (K40-era cuSPARSE); no full flags; first-party README. Baselines MKL/cuSPARSE are partly outside the listed baselines.
found_via: WebSearch: SpMV library faster than Intel MKL cuSPARSE sparse matrix-vector multiplication CSR format paper code github

name: CSR5 (Benchmark_SpMV_using_CSR5)
baseline: Intel MKL 11.2, cuSPARSE v6.5, CUSP, ViennaCL, BiCSB, pOSKI
workload: SpMV on irregular matrices across CPU, NVIDIA GPU, AMD GPU and Xeon Phi
claimed_speedup: Average improvement vs second-best method on irregular matrices: 17.6% (CPU), 28.5% (NVIDIA), 173.0% (AMD), 293.3% (Xeon Phi)
compiler_and_flags: Intel C/C++ 15.0.1 (x86), g++ 4.8.2 (GPU hosts), CUDA 6.5, OpenCL 1.2, OpenMP+AVX2; exact flags not seen
hardware: Dual Xeon E5-2667 v3; GTX 980; Radeon R9 290X; Xeon Phi 5110p
tradeoffs: New storage format (conversion cost from CSR); per-platform code folders
caveats: ICS 2015 paper, 2015-era library versions; flags not fully stated; baselines MKL/cuSPARSE not in the listed incumbents; commit date not checked.

name: AMGCL
workload: 3D Poisson problem on shared memory, AMG setup and solve times
claimed_speedup: Setup about 20-100% faster than Trilinos and 4-7 times faster than PETSc; slightly better than CUSP on GPU; distributed: about 3x slower than Trilinos AMG
hardware: Dual Intel Xeon E5-2640 v3; Tesla K80; MareNostrum 4, PizDaint, SuperMUC for distributed
tradeoffs: Header-only; OpenMP/OpenCL/CUDA backends; solver setup speed, not necessarily solve time
caveats: First-party docs; flags not stated; setup-phase speedup only, and distributed run is slower than Trilinos AMG; PETSc configuration not detailed on page.
found_via: WebSearch: algebraic multigrid library faster than PETSc hypre BoomerAMG open source C++ benchmark

name: BaSpaCho
workload: Batched supernodal sparse Cholesky for SPD matrices (bundle adjustment style, synthetic and BAL problems)
claimed_speedup: README claims state-of-the-art vs CHOLMOD and ships bench tools; no concrete numbers seen
tradeoffs: Supernodal only; README says simplicial/banded matrices better served by CHOLMOD or Eigen; GPU path needs CUDA
caveats: No numbers in README; tier D given with 112 stars (below notability bar, retained as relevant). Reproducible via bench -B 1_CHOLMOD.
found_via: WebSearch: sparse Cholesky LDL factorization library open source faster than CHOLMOD github C++ supernodal

name: Ginkgo
baseline: NVIDIA AmgX; MAGMA batched dense; MA57; LAPACK dgbsv
workload: GPU mixed-precision AMG, batched iterative solvers, sparse solves in AC-OPF
claimed_speedup: Mixed-precision AMG 1.5x faster than AmgX (20-40% on three larger problems); BatchBicgstab about 2x over MAGMA; 1.8-2.4x faster than MA57 on MI250X vs CPU
hardware: AMD MI250X, NVIDIA V100, Perlmutter, Crusher
caveats: Peer-reviewed (IJHPCA 2024) but baselines are not the listed SuiteSparse/Eigen/PETSc; paper itself has no direct PETSc or cuSPARSE comparison. Flags not stated.
found_via: WebSearch: Ginkgo sparse solver benchmark speedup over PETSc Trilinos

name: Sympiler
workload: Sparse triangular solve and Cholesky factorization via symbolic-analysis-decoupled code generation
claimed_speedup: Triangular solve average 3.8x over Eigen; Cholesky average 3.8x over Eigen and 1.5x over CHOLMOD (up to 6.3x vs Eigen in specific cases)
tradeoffs: Code generator specialised on a fixed sparsity pattern; needs symbolic inspection phase
caveats: SC17 paper numbers; repo license not confirmed on the page (LICENSE file path 404), so treated as reference; paper does not itself link a repo.
found_via: WebSearch: Sympiler OR sparse triangular solve OR sparse Cholesky code generation faster than Eigen MKL CHOLMOD

name: Task-based nested multithreaded CHOLMOD for A64FX (OmpSs)
workload: Sparse multithreaded Cholesky on 60 SuiteSparse matrices, 48-core A64FX
claimed_speedup: OPT-D-COST 1.95x average over mt-BLAS CHOLMOD across 60 matrices; 1.46x vs state-of-the-art task approach
tradeoffs: Requires OmpSs runtime and A64FX-specific tuning
caveats: Code is cited at a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.5974376) that I did not open, so has_code false and license unknown; niche ARM hardware.
found_via: WebSearch: sparse Cholesky LDL factorization library faster than CHOLMOD; arxiv.org/pdf/2202.09288
